questions.q: What is the key difference between the Data Map and the Unified Catalog?
options: They are two names for the exact same screen
The Data Map is the technical backbone that scans and catalogs real sources; the Unified Catalog is the business-facing layer organizing that metadata into domains, glossary terms, and data products
The Data Map is for compliance reporting; the Unified Catalog is for scanning data sources
The Unified Catalog replaced the Data Map and the Data Map no longer exists
questions.explain: The Data Map connects to, scans, and technically catalogs data sources. The Unified Catalog sits on top of it, making that metadata discoverable to business users through domains, glossary terms, and data products.

questions.q: How many Microsoft Purview accounts can a tenant normally have under standard quota rules?
options: Unlimited
Exactly one
Exactly ten
Zero — accounts must be created by Microsoft support
questions.explain: Under normal quota rules, you can only create one Microsoft Purview account per tenant. If your organization already has one, the creation wizard won't let you make a second.

questions.q: Which capability is enterprise-only, per this lesson's comparison table?
options: Browsing and searching data assets
Manually adding a description to an asset
Automated scanning for the hybrid data estate
Viewing the Catalog
questions.explain: Automated scans for the hybrid data estate, along with collections, automated classification, workflows, and support access, are all enterprise-only. The free version supports manual browsing and tagging only, via live view of a limited set of Azure sources.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of this lesson's practical levers for controlling Data Map capacity and cost?
options: Running incremental scans after the first full scan
Staggering scan schedules instead of running several at once
Disabling lineage extraction when it isn't needed
Permanently disabling all scanning for every data source
questions.explain: The practical levers are incremental scans, scoping scans, staggering schedules, reducing frequency, disabling unused lineage extraction, and cleaning up stale metadata — not disabling scanning entirely, which would defeat the Data Map's purpose.

questions.q: What are the two trigger options when you create a scan?
options: Run it once, or set up a recurring schedule
Export it or import it
Public or private
Manual-only or disabled
questions.explain: When creating a scan, the trigger decision is simple: run it once, or set up a recurring schedule with its own cadence.

questions.q: When registering a new data source, what two things do you choose that connect it into the domain/collection structure?
options: A username and password only
A domain, then a collection within it (or domain only)
A scan rule set and a classification only
A region and a pricing tier only
questions.explain: Registering a source means selecting a domain and then a collection inside it (or choosing 'Select domain only'), which determines where the source and its assets live in the Data Map hierarchy.

questions.q: According to the five-step flow for applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map, what comes immediately after 'Classifications found'?
options: Register asset
Labels applied
Scan asset
Create labels
questions.explain: The flow is: Create labels → Register asset → Scan asset → Classifications found → Labels applied. Classifications found is the trigger condition that leads directly to labels being applied.

questions.q: What does the thunderbolt icon next to a classification name indicate?
options: The classification failed to apply
It's a system classification, one of Purview's 200+ built-in classifications
The asset has been deleted
The classification was applied by a different Purview account
questions.explain: The thunderbolt icon marks a classification as a system classification — one of the 200+ built-in classifications Purview ships with, as opposed to a custom one you created yourself.

questions.q: Where are sensitivity labels created and managed?
options: In the Data Map's Annotation management section
In Microsoft Purview Information Protection, under Sensitivity labels
Only through PowerShell, with no portal option
Inside each individual scan rule set
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels are created and managed in Microsoft Purview Information Protection — a separate solution from the Data Map, though labels can extend into the Data Map.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say the History tab matters for trust, not just troubleshooting?
options: If anyone could silently edit an asset's classification with no record, a well-rated or certified asset wouldn't actually mean anything
History is only used to calculate storage costs
History automatically reverts any unauthorized edit
History is purely cosmetic and has no governance purpose
questions.explain: A permanent, timestamped log of every change is what makes curation claims (like a high rating or certification) credible — there's no hidden tampering.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what does current Purview documentation increasingly call this same feature?
options: A collection
A governance domain
A classification rule set
A scan rule set
questions.explain: Microsoft renamed the feature as Unified Catalog matured — "governance domain" is the newer label for the same "business domain" feature, same five types and rules.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT something Unified Catalog adds on top of Data Map's raw technical inventory, per the lesson?
options: Physical server hardware provisioning
Governance domains grouping data by business area
Data products and glossary terms giving curated meaning to assets
Lineage and estate-health insights
questions.explain: Unified Catalog adds business context — domains, data products, glossary terms, lineage, and insights — not infrastructure provisioning, which isn't a catalog concern at all.

questions.q: What happens if a Health Management Action is marked Resolved, but the underlying catalog issue is actually still there?
options: Nothing — the action stays marked Resolved permanently
The entire Purview account is flagged for an audit
The next scheduled health-management refresh reopens the action automatically
The assigned owner is automatically removed from all roles
questions.explain: Resolution isn't taken on faith — the next scheduled refresh re-checks the catalog, and the action reopens automatically if the issue hasn't actually been fixed.

questions.q: Which of the three lineage-reporting activity types does Azure Synapse NOT support, unlike Azure Data Factory?
options: Copy Data
Data Flow
Execute SSIS Package
Synapse supports all three identically
questions.explain: Synapse reports lineage from Copy Data and Data Flow activities, but not Execute SSIS Package, since Synapse pipelines don't run SSIS packages.

questions.q: How does the Catalog Adoption report differ from the Data Stewardship report covered in Lesson 26?
options: Catalog Adoption measures usage (searches, active users); Data Stewardship measures governance (curation, ownership)
They are two names for the exact same report
Catalog Adoption only works for Power BI sources
Data Stewardship requires a separate Purview license
questions.explain: Data Stewardship answers how governed the estate is; Catalog Adoption answers whether people are actually using the catalog — searches, active users, most-viewed assets.

questions.q: What does an approved access request become afterward, according to this lesson?
options: A tracked record showing the data source path, access type, requestor, and date — an audit trail
Nothing — approved requests are deleted immediately with no record kept
A permanent, unchangeable grant that can never be revoked
A new Azure subscription created automatically for the requestor
questions.explain: The request becomes a tracked self-service access policy record, which is what lets a governance team audit who has access to what, and who approved it, later.

questions.q: What is the first step in starting a new workflow in Purview?
options: A short form — enter a name and an optional description, then select Continue
Writing custom code in a script editor
Contacting Microsoft support to request a new workflow slot
Deleting all existing workflows first
questions.explain: Starting a workflow begins with a short form (name and description) rather than a blank canvas — Continue then opens the actual authoring canvas with a base template loaded.

questions.q: Which four sections does the Purview Solutions page group its offerings into?
options: Core, Risk & Compliance, Data Governance, and Data Security
Basic, Standard, Premium, and Enterprise
Windows, Azure, Microsoft 365, and Dynamics
Free, Trial, Paid, and Legacy
questions.explain: The Solutions page organizes everything into Core (shared setup), Risk & Compliance, Data Governance, and Data Security sections.

questions.q: What are the three self-check questions this lesson says you should be able to answer before moving on?
options: Find it (search the catalog), trace it (explain its lineage), and defend it (justify its label and rule)
Price it, ship it, and market it
Delete it, rebuild it, and rescan it
Name it, rename it, and archive it
questions.explain: The lesson's self-check is explicitly: can you find the asset in the catalog, trace its lineage out loud, and defend why its sensitivity label and data quality rule are the right choices.

questions.q: Is Thistledown Retail Group, the company in this case study, a real business?
options: No — it's explicitly described as a fictional, illustrative composite scenario
Yes — it is a real, named retail company
Yes — it is a real company whose name was changed for privacy
The lesson does not say whether it is real or fictional
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly labels Thistledown Retail Group as fictional and illustrative, consistent with this catalog's policy against presenting invented scenarios as real.

questions.q: What pattern does the lesson say the 'split author from publisher' habit reflects, beyond just Purview's policy feature?
options: A broader governance principle: a single person shouldn't be able to both write and activate a consequential change with no second set of eyes
A requirement that only exists for Azure Storage specifically
A rule that applies only to glossary terms and nothing else
A technical limitation that will be removed in a future Purview update
questions.explain: The lesson generalizes Lesson 28's Policy author / Data source admin split into a broader habit worth recognizing in approvals, classifications, and workflow templates generally.
